chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from an-Nadr from al-Qasim from Jarrah al-Mad'ani who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a father giving a gift to his child with evidence (as proof of gift), and he said: 'If he gives it to him while in good health, it is valid.'
ai.seo_question: Is a father's gift to his child during his lifetime valid if proven with evidence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms the validity of a father's gift to his child during health, provided there is clear evidence (bayyinah). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that such inter vivos gifts are not automatically considered part of the final estate distribution, thereby allowing parents to manage their wealth while alive without triggering the strict equal distribution rules of inheritance (mirath) that apply to bequests made near death.
